note: STEP 3b CLEAN: the table really is the 20-item PANAS and not one of the three sibling instruments in the same deposit. The paper's Instruments section names 'The PANAS (Watson, Clark & Tellegen, 1988)... Each scale is composed of 10 adjectives... on a five-point Likert scale from "not at all or very slightly" = 1 to "extremely" = 5', which fixes the variant as the original 20-item PANAS -- not the 60-item PANAS-X and not the 10-item I-PANAS-SF. The live sets confirm it: 20 items, resp 1-5, against the deposit's siblings OXH (29 items, 1-6), QL (26 items, 1-5) and SL (5 items, 1-7). CODE DERIVATION is core-model pattern 2, a number-preserving rename: data/medvedev_2018_wellbeing.py melts the explicit by-name column list [f'PAN{i}' for i in range(1,21)] and rewrites the code as 'pan_' + the trailing digits, so pan_N is workbook column PANN with no positional step. TEXT SOURCE: the deposit carries NO item text at any level -- headers are bare 'PAN1'..'PAN20', there are no Excel cell comments on row 1, it is .xlsx so there are no SPSS variable or value labels, and the article reproduces only three adjectives ('excited', 'interested', 'distressed') as examples. The 20 adjectives and the five anchors are therefore the canonical Watson et al. (1988) instrument, in its printed order, which is what makes the mapping reconstructed rather than data_labels. DEVIATIONS DISCLOSED: (a) instructions are left blank -- neither the paper nor the deposit reproduces the PANAS instruction paragraph, and it was not imported from the canonical form; (b) the paper prints only the two endpoint anchors and renders the bottom one as 'not at all or very slightly', whereas the canonical form reads 'very slightly or not at all' -- the canonical wording is shipped for all five anchors because the paper does not print anchors 2-4 at all, and mixing the study's endpoint rendering with canonical middles would produce a scale from no single source; (c) item_text is a bare adjective with no stem, which is the instrument's real shape (audit_batch.R's blank-stem WARN does not apply here since item_text is populated). RIGHTS: no block. The PANAS is the case SKILL.md names explicitly -- 'a bare copyright notice on a journal article is a notice about that article, not a term governing the instrument (the PANAS case)'. No fee, no-redistribution clause or stated use restriction from Watson, Clark & Tellegen is locatable to quote, and instrument_rights_register.csv carries no PANAS row; three PANAS tables shipped on 2026-09-08 on the same basis (kraft_todd_2017_panas, lee_2024_panas, liu_2018_panas). The deposit itself is CC BY 4.0. Note this is separate from the sibling medvedev_2018_ql, which is blocked -- that one is the WHOQOL-BREF, whose rights holder does state a redistribution bar. MAPPING VERIFIED TO CLASS: see verify_medvedev_2018_pan.R -- the study's own PANPOS/PANNEG/PANNEGR composites reproduce exactly (173/173, 172/172, 172/172) as raw sums of the canonical positive block {1,3,5,9,10,12,14,16,17,19} and negative block {2,4,6,7,8,11,13,15,18,20}, and the same identity holds computed from the LIVE pan_N codes (172/172 matched respondents). That pins every code's valence class but not its position within the class, so Step 5b status is PARTIAL.
